title: The Missing Notebook

beats.narrativeText: Buried in the archive is a reference nobody has followed up on until now: one final field notebook, belonging to Dr. Elara Quinn herself.
Only scattered pages of the notebook survive, and whole stretches of it are simply gone — not corrupted like the old logs, just missing.
The learner draws on journal entries, maps, timestamps and everything discovered across the whole campaign to begin reassembling the notebook.
Arranging the surviving pages into order finally starts to surface Dr. Quinn's own final recorded observations, in something close to her own words.

The learner must write the missing sections using the available evidence, and hold the line between a confirmed fact and a reasonable inference — a harder line to draw here than it's ever been before.
beats.trigger: Missing sections written and inference separated from fact

beats.narrativeText: The reconstructed notebook changes everything: the expedition wasn't hiding their discoveries at all. They were protecting them.
The learner reflects on how much can still be understood from a record this damaged — and how differently the whole expedition reads now that its purpose has changed.
Dr. Quinn's motivations are finally clear. The campaign shifts here — from piecing together what happened, to actually solving why it happened.

activities.title: Reassemble Notebook Pages
activities.storyContext: Only scattered pages remain of Dr. Elara Quinn's final field notebook — the closest thing to her own voice the expedition has left behind.
activities.instructions: Read the surviving notebook pages carefully and work out how they fit together, even where the connection isn't obvious at first.
activities.output: A reassembled order of the surviving notebook pages.

activities.title: Arrange Events Chronologically
activities.storyContext: Journal entries, maps, timestamps and everything discovered in earlier missions all hold clues to the correct order of events.
activities.instructions: Arrange the events described in the notebook into chronological order, cross-checking against what you've already learned from earlier missions.
activities.output: A chronological timeline of Dr. Quinn's final observations.

activities.title: Write Missing Sections Using Evidence
activities.storyContext: Large parts of the notebook are missing entirely — this is where everything the campaign has taught you gets used at once.
activities.instructions: Write the missing sections of the notebook, using evidence from the surviving pages and everything you've discovered across the whole expedition so far.
activities.output: Written reconstructions of the missing notebook sections.

activities.title: Distinguish Facts From Inference
activities.storyContext: Not everything written in the reconstructed notebook can be fully trusted — an inference can feel almost certain and still not be a fact.
activities.instructions: Sort your reconstruction into confirmed facts and reasonable inference, and be honest with yourself about which is which.
activities.output: Two lists: confirmed facts and reasonable inference.

activities.title: Write Another Perspective
activities.storyContext: Every expedition member would have experienced these events differently to Dr. Quinn.
activities.instructions: Write an additional journal entry from the perspective of another expedition member.
activities.output: A journal entry written from another expedition member's perspective.

activities.title: Reconstructing Incomplete Manuscripts
activities.storyContext: Reconstructing this notebook is similar to real historical research.
activities.instructions: Find out how archaeologists and historians reconstruct incomplete manuscripts.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What do you think Dr. Quinn was really trying to protect, and how is that different from what you originally assumed?

discussionPoints: What do you think Dr. Quinn was protecting, and why?
How did you decide what to write in the missing sections?
parentGuide.assessment: Look for missing sections that are reasonably supported by surrounding evidence, and a clear separation between confirmed facts and inference.

completionCriteria: Notebook pages reassembled, events arranged chronologically, and missing sections written using evidence.
